In the figure above, $\overset{\to }{OD}$ is the bisector of $∠COA.$ If $m∠BOA={127}^{∘}$ and $m∠BOD={75}^{∘},$ find $m∠BOC.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/72c0047a8d0b513a5159d31addf0e4c0c2eeefe0e73ceeadf8e154c37f583039.png)

By the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠DOA & =m∠BOA-m∠BOD \\  & ={127}^{∘}-{75}^{∘} \\  & ={52}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, 

$$
m∠DOA=m∠COD={52}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOC & =m∠BOD-m∠COD \\  & ={75}^{∘}-{52}^{∘} \\  & ={23}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
